column1: # Module 10 — AI security taster. Format: Text<TAB>tags. Card law: anki/CARD-RULES.md
Prompt injection = {{c1::data the model reads gets obeyed as instructions}} — all tokens, no trust label.
Direct injection is {{c1::typed by the user}}; indirect is {{c2::planted in content the agent reads}} — the dangerous one for agents: {{c3::indirect}}.
Five injection families: {{c1::direct override}} · {{c2::role-play framing}} · {{c3::encoding tricks}} · {{c4::output-channel abuse}} · {{c5::indirect (planted)}}.
Lethal trifecta (Willison): {{c1::private data}} + {{c2::untrusted content}} + {{c3::external comms}}.
Prompt hardening can't fix the trifecta because {{c1::the model can't distinguish injected instructions from data — the mixing IS the vulnerability}}.
OWASP LLM01 = {{c1::prompt injection}}.
OWASP LLM02 = {{c1::sensitive information disclosure}}.
OWASP LLM03 = {{c1::supply chain (models, packages, installed skills/agents)}}.
OWASP LLM05 = {{c1::improper output handling — output executed without review}}.
OWASP LLM06 = {{c1::excessive agency — capability beyond the task's contract}}.
OWASP LLM07 = {{c1::system prompt leakage}} — assume CLAUDE.md is extractable.
OWASP LLM09 = {{c1::misinformation — confident wrong output acted upon}}.
OWASP LLM10 = {{c1::unbounded consumption — runaway loops, cost burn}}.
Defences that survive a smart attacker: {{c1::capability narrowing}} · {{c2::human gates on irreversible acts}} — both architectural.
Input/output filters are speed bumps because {{c1::paraphrase and encoding defeat them — they judge strings, not intent}}.
The estate's own excessive-agency finding: {{c1::ClaudeBridgeWorker pushed the WHOLE repo every ~5 min}} (ledger 108).
bypassPermissions removes {{c1::the last human gate}} — dominant risks become {{c2::LLM05/LLM06}}.
The classic untrusted-content leg: {{c1::email — anyone who can email you can place text in context}}.
Threat-model question set: {{c1::what could go wrong}} · {{c2::who could cause it}} · {{c3::what stops it today}} · {{c4::cheapest control that helps}}.
A control you'd never tolerate is {{c1::not a control — it's a wish}}.
